title: The Yoneda lemma: witness isweq of yoneda_map_1 by the inverse natural transformation
intent: Prove the Yoneda lemma — that a natural transformation from the representable yoneda C c to a functor F is a weak equivalence onto F c — by supplying, via isweq_iso, an explicit inverse natural transformation (yoneda_map_2, the witness) and discharging the two inverse laws as separate, self-contained same-file lemmas.

parent.name: isweq_yoneda_map_1
parent.statement: Lemma isweq_yoneda_map_1 (C : category) (c : C) (F : functor C^op HSET) : isweq (yoneda_map_1 C c F).

children.name: yoneda_map_1_2
children.statement: Lemma yoneda_map_1_2 (C : category) (c : C) (F : functor C^op HSET) (alpha : hom _ (yoneda C c) F) : yoneda_map_2 _ _ _ (yoneda_map_1 _ _ _ alpha) = alpha.
children.closed_by: nat_trans_eq (C:=C^op) (has_homsets_HSET) reduces the natural-transformation equality pointwise, then rewrite <- nat_trans_ax and id_right f (lines 184-193); closes on its own

children.name: yoneda_map_2_1
children.statement: Lemma yoneda_map_2_1 (C : category) (c : C) (F : functor C^op HSET) (x : pr1 (F c)) : yoneda_map_1 _ _ _ (yoneda_map_2 _ _ _ x) = x.
children.closed_by: simpl, rewrite (functor_id F), apply idpath (lines 201-203); closes on its own

applicability.goal_shape: isweq f — a goal that a map f : X → Y is a weak equivalence — where a candidate inverse g : Y → X and the two homotopies ∏ x, g (f x) = x and ∏ y, f (g y) = y can be supplied; here f = yoneda_map_1 C c F : hom (yoneda C c) F → pr1 (F c) and g = yoneda_map_2 C c F
applicability.use_when: the inverse (witness) has an explicit constructible definition, and its two inverse laws factor into separate lemmas whose statements are self-contained; an extensionality principle (here nat_trans_eq / funextsec) reduces an equality of structured maps to pointwise equalities
applicability.avoid_when: the inverse is not constructible without a choice or classical axiom (then prove isweq by unfolding it and showing contractibility of fibres); the two inverse laws share a long common proof not worth duplicating into two lemmas; or the map is already a known equivalence (then make_weq with an existing isweq is shorter)

claims.claim: The parent isweq_yoneda_map_1 closes from the named witness and the two lemmas in a five-line proof: set (T:=yoneda_map_2 C c F) names the inverse, use isweq_iso creates the inverse-plus-two-homotopies goals, and the three bullets are closed by apply T, apply yoneda_map_1_2, apply yoneda_map_2_1 (lines 312-316).

Each child closes on its own without another same-file lemma: yoneda_map_1_2 turns the natural-transformation equality into a pointwise equation with nat_trans_eq ... has_homsets_HSET and closes with rewrite <- nat_trans_ax and id_right f (lines 184-193); yoneda_map_2_1 closes with rewrite (functor_id F) and idpath (lines 201-203).
The authors state that this is the Yoneda lemma in the section comment: 'Yoneda lemma: natural transformations from [yoneda C c] to [F] are isomorphic to [F c]' (lines 143-144).

The glue is 13 lines (305-317) with a 5-line proof body (312-316); the two children are 17 and 8 lines (178-194, 197-204); the longest chain of project items below the main theorem is 2 (isweq_yoneda_map_1 → yoneda_map_2 → yoneda_map_2_ax), while the two inverse-law lemmas each sit at depth 1.
claims.evidence: line counts of the copied file code/UniMath/CategoryTheory/yoneda.v (317-305+1=13; 194-178+1=17; 204-197+1=8); depth traced by hand from the parent site to yoneda_map_2 (lines 169-176) and its naturality lemma yoneda_map_2_ax (lines 154-167)

claims.claim: The same witness move — isweq_iso with an inverse and two homotopies — is used again in the same file to prove the Yoneda embedding is fully faithful: yoneda_fully_faithful applies isweq_iso (line 330) and closes its two homotopy goals inline (lines 332-345).

metrics.how_counted: parent = lines 305-317 of the copied file, of which the proof body between Proof. and Defined. is lines 312-316 (5); children = yoneda_map_1_2 (178-194), yoneda_map_2_1 (197-204)

consequences: The move creates exactly three obligations via isweq_iso: an inverse g and the two homotopies g ∘ f = id (section) and f ∘ g = id (retraction); each is discharged by a single apply to a named lemma. The witness yoneda_map_2 is a Definition that must first prove its own naturality, done by the sub-lemma yoneda_map_2_ax; if that definition changes, both the sub-lemma and the two inverse laws must be revisited. The inverse laws are stated for an arbitrary alpha (resp. x), so no unfixed witness appears inside any child (survey F rule 8).
